comparisons.analysis: Both support the same sex-work decriminalization legislation in their pre-primary questionnaires. The comparison does not infer their stance from incumbent/challenger status.
Both affirm housing access for unhoused or inadequately housed LGBTQ residents. This is a shared stated goal, not proof of identical detailed housing platforms.

Forrest foregrounds grassroots nurse and tenant organizing; Mosley foregrounds public-service and legislative advocacy experience. Both describe collective work, rather than mutually exclusive approaches.

Bowman and Ghebreghiorgis both explicitly support Medicare for All. Ghebreghiorgis's original response fills the previously missing fifth candidate voice in the recorded field; it is not evidence of identical implementation plans.
Both support a Green New Deal and discuss international dimensions. This agreement does not make every element of their foreign or industrial policy identical.

Bowman emphasizes inside-outside movement power; Ghebreghiorgis emphasizes collaborative interventions informed by special-education work. Both present organizing and community partnership as resources for governing.
